::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 9th 1882  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS  Pembroke College Oxford 60/14/97
:::

My dear [Mr Price](people/person_1208.qmd)

Mr [Walter Smith](people/person_1344.qmd) took the [Mozleys](organizations/other_108.qmd)’ business when [John Mozley](people/person_1065.qmd) died and [Charles](people/person_1063.qmd) retired.  He was trained at [Macmillans](organizations/other_111.qmd) and I think he knows his profession (or what ever it is to be called) thoroughly.[^1]  He is a gentleman and pleasant to deal with in all ways.  I do not know [the present Parker](people/person_2349.qmd), as my dealings were with [his father](people/person_1142.qmd), but I prefer Mr Smith greatly to J H P.  He is very straightforward and lets one understand what he is about, and I should call him rather cautious than enterprising.  He has had to feel his way a good deal, for old John Mozley had attended to nothing for years, and a foreman they took into partnership immediately went mad, and upset the arrangements- and they had to go on paying him as partner after he was in an asylum, till the firm could be dissolved.  

So poor Mr Smith has had a great deal against him but I think he has done well, and I am quite sure you may have full confidence in his honourable dealing.

He is a very good Churchman, and would think the work a great honor  I think it would be the making of him so that I hope you will see your way to giving the publication to him.

[Julian](people/person_1624.qmd) is getting through the winter well among his birds and his china painting.

With kindest regards to Mrs Price
yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: As well as being Sedleian Professor of Natural Philosophy Price was secretary to the delegates of the Oxford University Press 1873-84, and his enquiry about Smith seems to have been about employing him in this capacity.
